summary: This snapshot (Oct 30, 20:48 UTC) has one big fresh result: Lilly's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline, released Oct 28. It's a Phase 3 head-to-head of retatrutide 9 and 12 mg against semaglutide 2 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes. At 80 weeks, A1C fell 2.2 points with both retatrutide doses versus 1.8 with semaglutide. Weight fell 19.5–20.9% versus 9.4%. It's about 58 hours old, so it misses the 48-hour Lane C window. It's also a diabetes-only head-to-head, and those have underperformed for us, and mainstream outlets (USA Today, ABC, NY Post, Reuters, STAT) have covered it heavily. Use it as the 13:00 retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short, not a long-form. Long-form stays on Lane A in the playbook order. Stopping (SURMOUNT-4) and protein come first, then hair loss. Two new Lane A questions have fresh hooks: tirzepatide fatigue (Oct 30 news; the Zepbound label lists 5–7% vs 3% on placebo) and food noise/cravings (Diabetes Obes Metab food-purchase study, Oct 29). Body-worry Short ideas: the thyroid warning (Oct 27 scoping review on surveillance and detection bias), mood and anxiety (Oct 26 neuropsychiatric review plus a pharmacovigilance paper on semaglutide and panic attacks), gastroparesis versus normal slow digestion, and kidney stones and hydration. Upcoming catalyst: ObesityWeek, Nov 14–17 in Washington DC. Novo has said it will present CagriSema data there, so pre-plan Lane C. Rejected: '$99 GLP-1' and compounded-price pieces (Page Six, Forbes). Proceed with caution on: the 41% cancer-risk story (an observational June study that Medscape recirculated) and GLP-1s and eating disorders (MIT Tech Review, Psychiatric Times, Oct 30).

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 Phase 3 topline (Oct 28). A1C −2.2 points (both retatrutide doses) vs −1.8; weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4% at 80 weeks, adults with type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: 13:00 retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Say it's the first randomized Phase 3 head-to-head; these are topline results, not yet peer-reviewed; the trial was in type 2 diabetes (not obesity without diabetes); retatrutide isn't approved, and Lilly has moved its filing to Q1 2027. Give each arm's exact dose and the timeframe. Not a long-form: it's about 58 h old, past the 48 h Lane C window.
candidates.why_now: Lilly press release Oct 28, then a second wave Oct 29–30 (Medscape, EMJ, Scripps, FOX5). Retatrutide Shorts built on new Phase 3 data have been our top Shorts (268, 205).

evidence.source: Eli Lilly press release (via Google News)
evidence.signal: Official topline: greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of semaglutide 2 mg

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 lead-in; 335 vs 335 randomized; +14.0% regain from week 36 to week 88 on placebo) plus the Metabolites regain review (Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, next in the playbook queue. First sentence answers the title: most people regain a meaningful amount, and here's what the trial measured. Then cover what helps people who are continuing: protein, lifting, habits. 'Don't stop or change your medicine on your own' in every field.

candidates.angle: New Lane A question, a natural neighbour of Side Effects (our best minutes per impression, 0.89). Answer first: it's listed, it's uncommon, and it often comes alongside eating much less. Then cover what's worth checking with a clinician (low intake, protein, fluids, iron and B12), with no dosing.
